model.name: lebowski
model.notes: 877M ConvNeXt encoder, host-kept history, no RL residual. Checkpoint 6f5c8d09/ecc73f48. The model the G55 runs.

public_open_loop.condition: Measured. comma's public two-camera segments (openpilot CI data), native intrinsics and the device's own calibration, both cameras; every model on the same decoded frames. Truth is what the recording car did next: carState speed and acceleration, yaw rate from the device's cameraOdometry. Segments where the car never moves have no data. 45 segments from 23 cars (39 with movement).

public_closed_loop.condition: Measured. comma's worldmodel-4B generates each next frame at 5 Hz from 9 history frames, 5 recorded anchor frames and the car's pose; the model drives comma's ideal car (the requested curvature and acceleration happen at once) for 7.2 s from the recorded start. Distance is to the recording car's own path. One window per segment, nearest the middle, where the car holds at least 5 m/s for the window and the 4.8 s before it; segments with no such stretch are left out. Seeds 0 and 1, averaged per segment. 28 segments from 17 cars, one 7.2 s window each.

truck_open_loop.condition: Measured. The G55's recorded drives replayed as the truck runs the model: narrow camera only, road-plane warp to 1.45 m (plane:1.45). Truth is the truck's CAN speed and yaw rate. Window = unit. 4 windows: 3 on an earlier camera mount, 1 on the current mount; 2 at night.

truck_recovery.condition: Measured. The truck closed loop with a disturbance while the model drives; only the tests listed ran. 2° off heading: an extra 2°/s yaw for the first second. 18 windows (9 day, 9 night). 0.5 m off centre: an extra yaw-rate pulse, out and back over the first 2 s, that would move an uncorrected car 0.5 m sideways with no net heading change. 18 windows (9 day, 9 night).

limits: Open-loop scores compare a model's action with what the recording driver or car did; a model that drives differently but well is scored as wrong, and smoother, later actions (what comma's RL residual produces by design) score worse here. Measured on the 2026-10-27 deep dive: open-loop accuracy did not predict closed-loop driving.

Closed-loop numbers come from a generative world model, not a car. Nothing separates models before about 2 s; past about 4 s the recorded anchor frames pull every model back toward the recorded path, so 4 s is the primary horizon.
Intervals are 95% percentile bootstraps over units (segments or windows); segments from the same car are not independent, so the public intervals are somewhat narrow.
Paired deltas are model minus baseline on the units both have; wins count units where the model is better in the metric's direction.
Truck open loop pools few windows (camera mounts changed between drives); read it as a check that a model works on the truck's camera, not a ranking.
Truck closed loop: the steering and powertrain simulation is fitted to the G55, not validated on it in closed loop; the reference is the driver's own line, not the lane centre.

Recovery tests are disturbances rendered by the world model (yaw it renders; a one-frame jump it does not, so none is used). The braking-lead test is not built yet: the drives the truck closed loop can use hold no window where a car ahead brakes.
